notes.front: What is the Department of Transportation (DOT), as it appears in the Section 608 test topics?
notes.back: The transport department whose approval and classification tag the test topics name for refrigerant cylinders.
notes.explanation: The test topics bring it in twice: once for approving reusable cylinders and once for the classification tag on shipping labels.
notes.example: Like a transport authority whose approval mark a container must carry before it is used.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: What is a self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA), in the Section 608 test topics?
notes.back: Breathing protection listed as personal protective equipment for extreme cases, after gloves and goggles.
notes.explanation: The test topics end their protective equipment list with it and limit it to extreme cases.
notes.example: Like the breathing set a firefighter wears into a smoke-filled building.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Personal protective equipment [gloves, goggles, self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA)-in extreme cases, etc.]

notes.front: In the Section 608 test topics, what is a recovery cylinder?
notes.back: A reusable refrigerant cylinder: the test topics call it “reusable (or ‘recovery’)”.
notes.explanation: The two names mark the same cylinder, which the test topics set against disposable cylinders.
notes.example: Like a refillable water bottle, as against a single-use one.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: In the Section 608 test topics, what is a disposable cylinder?
notes.back: A single-use refrigerant cylinder: the opposite of a reusable recovery cylinder.
notes.explanation: The test topics set the two cylinder types side by side and give each its own rules.
notes.example: Like a single-use camping gas canister, as against a refillable gas bottle.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: What are two risks of exposure to refrigerant that the test topics list?
notes.back: For example, oxygen deprivation and cardiac effects. Frostbite and long-term hazards are also listed.
notes.explanation: The list opens with “e.g.”, so it gives examples rather than every risk.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of exposure to refrigerant (e.g., oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects, frost bite, long-term hazards)

notes.front: Besides cardiac effects, frostbite and long-term hazards, the test topics list {{c1::oxygen deprivation}} as a risk of exposure to refrigerant.

notes.explanation: It is the first of the four examples the test topics give of exposure risks.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of exposure to refrigerant (e.g., oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects, frost bite, long-term hazards)

notes.front: Besides oxygen deprivation, frostbite and long-term hazards, the test topics list {{c1::cardiac effects}} as a risk of exposure to refrigerant.
notes.back: cardiac effects
notes.explanation: It is the second of the four examples the test topics give of exposure risks.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of exposure to refrigerant (e.g., oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects, frost bite, long-term hazards)

notes.front: Besides oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects and long-term hazards, the test topics list {{c1::frostbite}} as a risk of exposure to refrigerant.
notes.back: frostbite
notes.explanation: It is the third of the four examples the test topics give of exposure risks.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of exposure to refrigerant (e.g., oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects, frost bite, long-term hazards)

notes.front: Which of these is not among the refrigerant exposure risks the test topics list?
notes.back: Hearing loss.
notes.choices:
A) Oxygen deprivation
B) Cardiac effects
C) Hearing loss
notes.choicesExplained: A and B: both appear in the test topics’ list of exposure risks, alongside frostbite and long-term hazards.
notes.explanation: The test topics’ examples are oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects, frostbite and long-term hazards; hearing loss is not one of them.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of exposure to refrigerant (e.g., oxygen deprivation, cardiac effects, frost bite, long-term hazards)

notes.front: What are two items of personal protective equipment the test topics list for refrigerant work?
notes.back: Gloves and goggles. A self-contained breathing apparatus is added for extreme cases.
notes.explanation: The list ends in “etc.”, so it is not complete; the breathing apparatus is limited to extreme cases.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Personal protective equipment [gloves, goggles, self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA)-in extreme cases, etc.]

notes.front: The test topics list an SCBA as protective equipment {{c1::in extreme cases}}.
notes.back: in extreme cases
notes.explanation: Gloves and goggles come first in the list; the breathing apparatus is the item the test topics qualify.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Personal protective equipment [gloves, goggles, self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA)-in extreme cases, etc.]

notes.front: A technician is about to connect hoses for an ordinary recovery job. Which protective equipment from the test topics fits?
notes.back: Gloves and goggles; the test topics keep the SCBA for extreme cases.
notes.choices:
A) Gloves and goggles
B) An SCBA and nothing else
C) No protection is needed for routine work
notes.choicesExplained: B: the test topics limit the SCBA to extreme cases and list gloves and goggles first. C: the test topics list protective equipment as part of safety for this work.
notes.explanation: An ordinary hook-up is not an extreme case, so the first items on the list apply.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Personal protective equipment [gloves, goggles, self-contained breathing apparatus (SCBA)-in extreme cases, etc.]

notes.front: Whose approval must a reusable recovery cylinder have, according to the test topics?
notes.back: The Department of Transportation (DOT).
notes.explanation: The test topics attach the approval requirement to the reusable type, alongside its colour code.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: What colour code do the test topics give for reusable recovery cylinders?
notes.back: Yellow and grey.
notes.explanation: Technicians are expected to know the reusable type’s colours; the test topics give no colour for disposable cylinders.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: What must never be done with a disposable cylinder?
notes.back: Refill it.
notes.explanation: The test topics’ rule for disposable cylinders is short: never refill them, in contrast with reusable recovery cylinders.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: Above what fill level do the test topics flag risks for a refrigerant cylinder?
notes.back: More than 80 percent full.
notes.explanation: The test topics list the risks of filling past this point as a safety topic in their own right.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of filling cylinders more than 80 percent full

notes.front: A technician needs a cylinder to hold refrigerant recovered on a job. Which fits the test topics’ guidance?
notes.back: A reusable recovery cylinder that is DOT approved, marked with the yellow and grey colour code.
notes.choices:
A) A DOT-approved recovery cylinder with the yellow and grey code
B) An emptied disposable cylinder
C) Any container with a valve
notes.choicesExplained: B: the test topics say never to refill disposable cylinders. C: the test topics call for a DOT-approved reusable cylinder, not any container.
notes.explanation: The test topics require the reusable type to be DOT approved and to carry the yellow and grey code, and forbid refilling disposables.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: A disposable cylinder of R-134a is empty after a job. May the technician refill it with recovered refrigerant?
notes.back: No. The test topics say never to refill disposable cylinders.
notes.choices:
A) No, never refill a disposable cylinder
B) Yes, if it held the same refrigerant
C) Yes, up to 80 percent full
notes.choicesExplained: B: the test topics give no same-refrigerant exception. C: the 80 percent point concerns filling cylinders in general; it does not make refilling a disposable cylinder allowed.
notes.explanation: Recovered refrigerant goes into a reusable recovery cylinder; the empty disposable one is not reused.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]

notes.front: While recovering, a technician sees the recovery cylinder is about to pass 80 percent full. What does the test-topic guidance point to?
notes.back: Stop filling it and use another cylinder, since the test topics flag risks in filling past 80 percent.
notes.choices:
A) Stop filling and use another cylinder
B) Fill it to the top to save a trip
C) Vent some vapour and keep filling
notes.choicesExplained: B: filling past 80 percent is exactly what the test topics flag as risky. C: venting refrigerant breaks the Clean Air Act prohibition on venting.
notes.explanation: The 80 percent line is the point beyond which the test topics say filling a cylinder carries risks.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Risks of filling cylinders more than 80 percent full

notes.front: Which gas do the test topics say to use for leak detection, rather than oxygen or compressed air?
notes.back: Nitrogen.
notes.explanation: The test topics rule out both oxygen and compressed air for this job and name nitrogen instead.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Use of nitrogen rather than oxygen or compressed air for leak detection

notes.front: A technician wants to pressurise a system to hunt for a leak and has oxygen, compressed air and nitrogen on the van. Which do the test topics point to?
notes.back: Nitrogen.
notes.choices:
A) Nitrogen
B) Oxygen
C) Compressed air
notes.choicesExplained: B and C: the test topics say to use nitrogen rather than oxygen or compressed air for leak detection.
notes.explanation: The test topics name nitrogen for leak detection and rule out the other two.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Use of nitrogen rather than oxygen or compressed air for leak detection

notes.front: Which two items do the test topics say to use with nitrogen?
notes.back: A pressure regulator and a relief valve.
notes.explanation: The test topics list them together, right after the item on using nitrogen for leak detection.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Use of pressure regulator and relief valve with nitrogen

notes.front: A technician is about to connect a nitrogen cylinder straight to a system, with no regulator or relief valve. What does the test-topic guidance require?
notes.back: Fit a pressure regulator and a relief valve first.
notes.choices:
A) Fit a pressure regulator and a relief valve
B) Nothing: nitrogen needs no extra equipment
C) Swap the nitrogen for compressed air
notes.choicesExplained: B: the test topics list a regulator and relief valve for use with nitrogen. C: the test topics rule out compressed air for leak detection.
notes.explanation: The test topics call for both items whenever nitrogen is used.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Use of pressure regulator and relief valve with nitrogen

notes.front: What must a refrigerant cylinder’s label show about the cylinder’s contents?
notes.back: The refrigerant’s identification.
notes.explanation: It is one of the two label items the test topics require for refrigerant cylinders under shipping.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Shipping”
notes.evidence: Shipping - Labels required for refrigerant cylinders (refrigerant identification, DOT classification tag)

notes.front: Which Department of Transportation item must a refrigerant cylinder’s label carry for shipping?
notes.back: The DOT classification tag.
notes.explanation: It is the second label item the test topics require, beside the refrigerant’s identification.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Shipping”
notes.evidence: Shipping - Labels required for refrigerant cylinders (refrigerant identification, DOT classification tag)

notes.front: A technician is shipping a recovery cylinder of used R-22 to a reclaimer. What labels do the test topics call for?
notes.back: The refrigerant identification (R-22) and the DOT classification tag.
notes.choices:
A) Refrigerant identification and the DOT classification tag
B) No label, as the reclaimer will test it
C) Only the owner’s name
notes.choicesExplained: B: the test topics require labels for refrigerant cylinders. C: the required items are the refrigerant identification and the DOT classification tag.
notes.explanation: Both label items apply to any refrigerant cylinder being shipped, including recovered refrigerant going for reclamation.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Shipping”
notes.evidence: Shipping - Labels required for refrigerant cylinders (refrigerant identification, DOT classification tag)

notes.front: How do reusable recovery cylinders and disposable cylinders differ in the test topics?
notes.back: Recovery cylinders are reusable, DOT approved and coloured yellow and grey. Disposable cylinders must never be refilled.
notes.explanation: The test topics give the reusable type approval and colour rules, and give the disposable type one rule only.
notes.source: EPA, Section 608 Technician Certification Test Topics, “Core: Safety”
notes.evidence: Reusable (or "recovery") cylinders versus disposable cylinders [ensure former Department of Transportation (DOT) approved, know former's yellow and gray color code, never refill latter]
